workflow_runs.display_title: feat(agents): save native canvas node positions with the Agent

head_commit.message:
feat(agents): save native canvas node positions with the Agent

A drop on the native Agent canvas becomes a move_nodes graph command that
writes the document's display-only layout (skeleton_execution 1.10,
document_layout_v1). The move marks the draft unsaved, Save keeps it, undo
takes it back, and it travels with the Agent. Without that runtime the
canvas keeps the previous localStorage-only behaviour.

Adds the local mirror of the closed layout shape, pruning on delete, a
capture recorded from the real 1.10 validator, the sidecar store round trip
and the contract doc (BC-NL-001/002, SEQ-NL-001).

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(ui): keep switch thumb shadows in sync with thumb motion

head_commit.message:
fix(ui): keep switch thumb shadows in sync with thumb motion

ShadowSurface paints a detached, anchor-positioned SVG shadow that copies
the owner's transition, so it re-eases the thumb's already-eased slide and
trails behind it; it also falls back to the native shadow whenever the
thumb is scaled, so the glass puck's hover spring popped between two
shadows. Switch thumbs now paint a native box-shadow on the moving element
itself (glass, plain, semi and material variants).

glass switch, with the controls on one pair of edges. The default tool line is
no longer restated, removing moved inside the open row, and adding is one
control with a search and the embedded Agent as its last choice.

head_commit.message:
Make Agents a side-menu drill-in instead of a modal

The side menu's Agents entry now slides the menu into an Agents pane
("‹ Chats" goes back) and swaps the window's centre for the Agents
workspace. The agent list renders in that pane through a portal; the
graph canvas and detail panel fill the content area. The chat stays
mounted underneath, so a running stream and the input draft survive the
trip, and the workspace stays mounted once visited, so returning lands on
the same agent.

- NavigationContext carries appMode and the side-menu slot element
- RecipesPage gains a docked mode (explorerSlot / explorerDocked)
- AgentsModal and its test are removed; nothing opens it any more
- New chat from the Agents pane returns to the chat

head_commit.message:
fix(builder): let an input row wrap at the panel's minimum width

At the detail panel's 300px minimum an input row's header line
`[name] ← [source] ×` needs about 328px of the 248px it has, so the
agent and End bodies scrolled sideways and the source selector and
remove button sat past the edge (#341 acceptance, four shell units).

The header may now wrap: the name keeps the first line and `← source ×`
moves whole to the next one as one unshrinkable group. Nothing is
hidden, shrunk or clipped and the minimum width is unchanged; at wider
panels the line renders exactly as before.

head_commit.message:
chore(codeql): clear 48 code-scanning alerts on the sidecar and renderer

Dead module constants and unused imports are removed, modules imported
both as `import x` and `from x import y` keep one form, re-exported names
that tests and sibling modules read through routes.py and memory_factory
are declared in __all__, the raising helpers are typed NoReturn, a
request-provided toolkit name is stripped of line breaks before logging,
and two JavaScript sites drop a redundant null compare and a dead
assignment. No behaviour change; three names first removed turned out to
be module re-exports (character_defaults, REDACTION_MARKER) and stay.

workflow_runs.display_title: refine(agents): separate modal close from panel toggles

head_commit.message:
refine(agents): separate modal close from panel toggles

The Agents modal's close button shared its corner with the detail panel and
closed the panel first, so users could not tell whether it would close the
whole modal. Close now always closes the modal; each floating panel gets its
own toggle icon.

- Left list: full height; header row is the list toggle plus a "+" menu
  (New Agent / New Folder); search sits on its own row, styled like the root
  side menu's search.
- Detail panel: mirrored side_menu_right toggle in its header.
- macOS fullscreen: the header row steps right of the traffic lights instead
  of dropping below them.
- Theme: modal corner radius 12 -> 14.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
security: fix 39 CodeQL alerts and pin the release-QA Unchain ref

- session_guard_migration: read the pending intent through an
  O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW descriptor instead of exists-then-read (fs race)
- test-api /v1/debug/dom: embed the selector as a JS string literal
- route_computer_use: log on/off literals instead of request values
- release-qa fake provider / test-api client: fixed error body,
  validated port file
- memory_vault, vault_sink_job_supervisor, memory_v2_store:
  missing-await, exit-from-finally, implicit SQL concatenation
- _shared-release-deterministic.yml: refuse a UNCHAIN_SOURCE_REF that
  is not a full 40-hex commit SHA
- note-level cleanups: abstract-method docstrings, _OwnedHandle as a
  context manager, unused imports/locals, ASI, dead guards

Local CodeQL (security-and-quality): 302 -> 263 results, no new ones.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
fix(gemini): let a retired model reach Google so its 404 names the replacement (#386)

A chat or recipe that still names a removed 2.5 model failed locally with a
misleading "8192-token context window" error, because a model missing from the
catalog resolved to an unknown window. Unknown Gemini ids now use the Gemini
family's catalog window, so the request is sent and Google's 404 reaches the
user through the closed provider diagnostic, which names the replacement.

Refs #386

workflow_runs.display_title: Keep known token usage totals when some receipts have unavailable usage

head_commit.message:
fix(token-usage): keep known totals when some receipts have unavailable usage

Settings → Token Usage showed `—` for consumed, input, output and average
tokens and drew no chart whenever a single provider call in the selected
window had unknown usage: useTokenUsageData discarded every total as soon as
one record carried a non-numeric count, while the request count kept
counting all of them.

Sum each metric over the records where it is known, report the number of
excluded requests under the Overview grid, and give an all-unavailable
window its own chart empty state so it stays distinct from an empty window.
The run-bundle projection, IPC envelope and legacy storage are unchanged.

Refs #377

workflow_runs.name: CodeQL
workflow_runs.display_title: Render streamed reasoning deltas as one block per model turn

head_commit.message:
fix: render streamed reasoning deltas as one block per model turn

Anthropic-protocol providers emit one reasoning runtime event per
thinking_delta, and each became its own trace frame. On DeepSeek every
delta is a single token, so one reasoning turn rendered as hundreds of
"Reasoning" blocks and inflated the step count.

Coalesce adjacent reasoning delta frames from the same run and iteration
in TraceChain's displayFrames. This covers live streams and already
persisted chats. Whole Responses API reasoning_items stay separate.

Refs #379

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

workflow_runs.display_title: feat: add CODEOWNERS and the code owner path

head_commit.message:
feat: add CODEOWNERS and the path to becoming a code owner

Introduces the delegation mechanism designed in
docs/plans/2026-09-29-code-owner-path-design.md.

CODEOWNERS starts with a fallback line assigning every unclaimed path to the
project owner, plus the paths that are never delegated: the release workflows,
CODEOWNERS itself, the MCP store catalog, and the legal files. Assigned areas
are appended one line at a time as applications are approved.

docs/contributing/becoming-a-code-owner.md states the bar publicly: two merged
pull requests in the path applied for, an issue to apply, and the two ways the
role lapses. A code owner may approve and merge inside their path, including
their own changes; main, the release pipeline, and the store catalog are never
delegated.

This file has no effect until require_code_owner_review is enabled on the
branch rulesets.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
docs: drop the Discussions channel from the contributor path

Discussions was added as the optional expression-of-interest channel, but an
inbox nobody intends to watch is worse than no inbox: an unanswered thread
reads as an inactive project.

Interest now arrives as a comment on the issue itself, which is where claiming
already happens, so a task keeps one canonical home and no second surface needs
watching. Questions about a task go on that task. Setup problems and unsure
ideas open an issue.

Removes both Discussions contact links, leaving three guide links on the issue
chooser, and removes the Discussions references from README, CONTRIBUTING, and
the first-contribution guide.

workflow_runs.display_title: docs: add an onboarding path for external contributors

head_commit.message:
docs: add an onboarding path for external contributors

Newcomers had no starting point: the README presented the MCP store as the
only way in, nothing defined `good first issue` or `help wanted`, no rule said
how a task is claimed, and there was no channel for "I'd like to help".

Add docs/contributing/first-contribution.md as the single page all entry points
lead to, covering contribution types, finding and claiming a task, setup, the
base: dev submission flow, and what a contributor explicitly does not need
(write access, label permissions, board access).

Document the claiming rule identically there and in CONTRIBUTING.md: comment to
claim, a maintainer assigns, 14 days without visible progress releases it.

Route interest and questions to Discussions from the issue-creation screen
rather than onto the issue tracker, matching the convention in comparable
projects. Add CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md (Contributor Covenant 2.1).

Repair the README anchor to CONTRIBUTING.md, dead since that heading was
renamed to "Contribute an MCP server, Skill, or Toolkit".

Closes #315

head_commit.message:
fix(agents): category glyphs for the palette, and two menu icon calls (#358)

- The palette's groups carry their own glyph: a route for Steps, the things
  that move the flow along, and a puzzle piece for Attachments, the things that
  hang off a node. Declared in the catalog next to the labels, so a new group
  cannot arrive without one — a test asserts every group has an icon and that
  the key exists in the manifest.
- Select all takes shape-line, the four-handled selection box.
- Fit to view loses its glyph. It and Reset zoom are view plumbing rather than
  actions on the graph, and they now read as a quiet pair: no shortcut and no
  icon on either.

Icons added from Remix Icon: route (Map/route-line), puzzle_2
(Development/puzzle-2-line), shape (Design/shape-line). No SVG was drawn by
hand.

Verified in the running app against an isolated profile: the palette's STEPS
heading renders the route glyph, and the seven corrections from the previous
commit all hold — no menu mid-drag, the detail page closes when its node is
deleted, the view rows are bare, ⌘ draws from the manifest, doorway rows carry
the chevron, Duplicate is gone, and the palette footer uses corner-down-left.

workflow_runs.display_title: feat(agents): target-aware canvas context menus and a node palette (#358)

head_commit.message:
feat(agents): give the canvas a menu per right-click target, and a node palette (#358)

The canvas had one context menu and it was the same everywhere: onContextMenu
sat on the container and reported only coordinates, so right-clicking a node, a
connection or empty space all opened the same three-item "Add" list, and
nothing on it acted on what was clicked.

Resolve the target inside the existing handler — nodes already carry
data-flow-node-id, and the edge hit path now carries data-flow-edge-id — select
it, and pass it through. No new editor API.

- recipe_node_catalog.js: one entry per addable node type (label, group, icon,
  description, ports, creation defaults, id prefix, graph_kinds). ports_for,
  add_node and the palette all read it, so the palette cannot offer a node that
  creation does not know how to build. Graph-kind filtering is written now and
  inert until a recipe carries a kind.
- Three menu builders plus a dispatcher. Groups are fixed, membership varies by
  capability. Delete reads node.deletable, the flag the Delete key already
  reads, so keyboard and menu cannot disagree; Start and End grey out with the
  reason in the row's new trailing slot.
- recipe_node_palette.js: search, grouped results, arrow keys and Enter,
  Escape and click-away. Inserts where the right-click happened.
- recipe_graph_edits.js: "Insert node after…" and "Insert node here…" splice
  into the flow rather than dropping a floating node — outer ports preserved,
  attach connections and non-flow nodes refused.
- ContextMenu: rows gain a trailing slot (shortcut when enabled, reason when
  disabled), and measureMenuHeight replaces items.length * 32, which counted a
  9px separator as a 32px row. The side menu's and recipe list's menus already
  use separators, so they overstated their height and flipped upward early near
  the window bottom; they sit correctly now.
- Escape with a menu or the palette open no longer closes the Agents modal
  underneath it: the menu closes on a document listener, Modal closes on a
  window listener, and the menu is not on the modal stack.
- FlowEditor gains fit_token, zoom_reset_token and select_all_token following
  the existing reset_token idiom, starting undefined so they stay inert on
  mount.

Rename is deliberately absent rather than dead: only the agent node renders a
name today, and the per-type identity table in #341 replaces these node
components, so building inline rename now would mean building it twice. The
builder shows the row only when a handler is supplied.

Tests: 430 suites / 5239 passed on this candidate; base f9c870e6 measured
425 / 5162. CI build compiles clean. Verified in the running app against an
isolated profile.

head_commit.message:
fix(agents): cap each builder panel at a share of the canvas (#339)

The workflow list and the detail panel stopped at fixed widths (480 and
640), which is a different thing on a laptop and on a large display: on a
small window either panel could take almost everything, while on a wide
one neither could use the space.

Each panel now has a share of the canvas instead: the list 35% and the
detail panel 50% (project owner, 2026-09-26). The minimum stays absolute
(200 / 300) and wins when the share falls below it, so a narrow window
keeps the panel usable rather than squeezing it.

- recipe_panel_widths: RECIPE_PANEL_LIMITS carries maxRatio in place of
  max, with panelMaxWidth() and clampPanelWidth() to apply it.
  readRecipePanelWidths() takes an optional container width, so a width
  stored when the window was wider comes back inside the new share.
- recipes_page: measures the canvas with a ResizeObserver, falling back to
  the window's width while the box reports 0 (first paint, jsdom) rather
  than collapsing every panel to its minimum. A container that shrinks
  pulls the panels back in.

Measured live at a 918px canvas: the list stops at 323px (35.2%) and the
detail panel at 461px (50.2%); the extra fraction is each panel's 6px
inset from the edge.

Tests: 423 suites / 5154 passed. GitNexus detect-changes: 4 files,
18 symbols, 6 flows, risk high — every affected flow is RecipesPage's own
panel-width path.

head_commit.message:
fix: remove six more provably dead CodeQL findings

_characters_dir in memory_factory joined the dead duplicates removed in the
previous commit: deleting its two callers left it with no use before the late
re-import that overwrites it, which is how the alert surfaced (#401).

use_message_window_scroll picked `is_streaming ? "auto" : "smooth"` in an
effect whose streaming branch returns twenty lines earlier, so it could only
ever choose "smooth" (#360). Streaming's bottom-follow is scheduled in that
branch; the ternary suggested a second streaming path that does not exist.

plugin_trust_badge guarded resolvePluginTrust with `|| {}` (#361). That
function builds and returns a complete projection on every path, a rejected
entry included, so the guard was unreachable and obscured the contract.

windows-installed-sink-matrix bound the cold-restart relaunch to a local
`page` nothing reads afterwards (#358); runCell takes its handle from app.page,
which launch() republishes. custom_provider_editor initialised savedSlug to a
value always overwritten before first read, the catch included (#359).

character_seeding tested `changed or current_seed_version != target_seed_version`
after a branch that returns for every registry already at the target, so the
right half could not be false (#203). The save is unconditional; the test made
the seeding loop's return value look load-bearing when nothing read it.

Not fixed, verified false positives: #363 (the count guard IS reachable — the
effect sets mountedWindowCount to the cap, after which the two counts are
equal); #296 (DurableInteractionReceiptResult subclasses dict so it serialises
as the public result, and an __eq__ including the private handoff would break
comparison against an expected payload); #204-#210 (`...` bodies on
@abstractmethod are deliberate style, not ineffectual statements).

electron 8834 passed/576 suites; release-qa unit 395 passed/5 skipped; the
Windows-only sink matrix is node --check only on this platform.

blast radius of the hook and the editor, not of the change, every edit being

head_commit.message:
fix: clear 32 CodeQL alerts, including a dead SQL-degradation switch

skill_folder_storage declared a per-session degradation switch and a comment
saying a known-bad SQL write path stays on localStorage until the next boot,
but nothing ever set the flag (js/trivial-conditional #362). The agent store
trips its copy from the legacy-seed failure path; this store has no seed, so
a persistent SQL failure logged a warning and stored the tree nowhere — the
repository had already rolled the namespace back. saveRaw now degrades on a
rejected write and deposits the tree in localStorage on the way down, because
this namespace is new and has nothing to fall back TO. Red-before-green: both
new tests fail against the previous implementation.

toolkit_icon passed isDark to getToolkitIconBackground, which takes the icon
alone (#390). A builtin icon's plate colour comes off the icon manifest and
has no dark variant, so the argument was dropped on the floor from the start.

src/setupTests.js joins the CodeQL paths-ignore. It is the Jest bootstrap, not
shipped code, and in scope it made CodeQL resolve every
`new ResizeObserver(callback)` in the app to the jsdom mock defined there —
whose implicit constructor takes no arguments — reporting 25 correct call
sites as superfluous-argument alerts.

memory_factory drops three duplicate definitions that the late re-imports at
the bottom of the module overwrite before first use (#197/#198/#199); the
surviving implementations in memory_paths/memory_storage are equivalent.
_normalize_optional_threshold loses an unreachable `numeric < 0` branch
(#211) and gains the guard that was actually missing: NaN fails every
comparison there, so it reached round() and came back out as a NaN threshold.

unchain_adapter._optimizer_float replaces `not (parsed == parsed) or parsed in
(inf, -inf)` with math.isfinite (#202) — same set, minus an idiom that reads
as a tautology and invites deletion.

head_commit.message:
fix(security): make the log and fingerprint guards hold at the descriptor

The log sanitizer now removes carriage returns and newlines explicitly before
the control-character pass. Stripping them is what stops a request-supplied
identifier from forging a second entry in any consumer that reads the log as
lines, and saying so directly is also what the analyzer recognizes.

The worktree fingerprint opens each untracked path first and describes that
descriptor, instead of stat-ing the path and then reading it: the two calls
could be handed different inodes, and this digest is the evidence that a
worktree did not change. A symlink is now detected by O_NOFOLLOW failing the
open rather than by a prior stat.

Verified: 2477 sidecar tests pass, release-qa unit suite green, and the
fingerprint stays deterministic and change-sensitive over a real tree holding
a file, a symlink and an empty directory.

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(security): stop returning internal exception text to the renderer

head_commit.message:
fix(security): stop returning internal exception text to the renderer

Nineteen generic `except Exception` fallbacks across the Flask routes put
`str(exc)` in the response body. That text is an internal detail — a
filesystem path, a JSON offset, an OS or driver error — and the renderer
persists it with the chat. Each one now returns its stable error code with a
fixed message and logs the exception server-side instead.

route_characters carried nine of them and logged nothing at all, so an
internal failure was both leaked to the client and lost from the server log;
it gains a logger and one shared helper. route_recipes, route_projection,
route_memory and route_computer_use follow the same shape. The MCP OAuth
callback page renders in the user's default browser and could show the MCP
server's own stderr (issue #249), so it now shows the error code only.

Deliberate messages are untouched: `except ValueError` validation text, the
coded domain errors that carry status and retryable, and route_providers,
which already passes its text through redact_text.

Two request-supplied identifiers reaching a log format string are bounded and
stripped of control characters first — a newline in one forges a second entry
in any consumer that reads the log as lines.

CodeQL also stops scanning `**/__fixtures__/**`: captured upstream pages are
data the tests replay, not code this project ships.

Verified: 2477 sidecar tests pass. GitNexus detect-changes reports HIGH risk
over 9 execution flows; no route changed its status code or error code, only
the message text and the logging.

The live-run credentials loader checked the 0600 mode of a path and then read
that path, so a file could pass the permission guard while the bytes came from
something else — and the guard exists to protect provider API keys. The mode
check and the read now share one descriptor.

The qualification feed writes its output with "wx" instead of testing
existence first.

head_commit.message:
fix(security): close ten high CodeQL findings

Path traversal out of the tool-media root (2 alerts, the serious pair):
`_safe_session_component` allowed "." and ".." through its character
allowlist, so `media_root / ".."` was the data directory itself. `_sweep_dir`
deletes every file older than the TTL in the directory it is handed and
`sweep_session` runs at stream start and end, so a session id of ".." would
have reclaimed chats.db and settings.db. Dot-only components now resolve to
the no-session bucket, and `_session_dir` additionally asserts containment so
a later change to the sanitizer cannot silently reopen the escape.

Time-of-check/time-of-use file races (8 alerts): each site now performs its
check and its read through one file handle, or drops a check that told it
nothing. Skill scanning reads first and bounds the string afterwards (the
oversized branch already read the whole file, so the stat only added a
window). Windows signing evidence, the worktree fingerprint, the pricing JSON
loader and the source-capture body all stat the open descriptor they read
from — these produce release and pricing evidence, so a swapped path must not
be able to keep a digest or a size check looking valid. The worktree
fingerprint also opens with O_NOFOLLOW. The qualification fixture config
writes with "wx" instead of testing existence first.

Verified: electron 8834, frontend 5116, sidecar 2477 (12 of them new media
containment cases, including that a ".." session can no longer sweep the data
directory), pricing-catalog and release-qa unit suites all pass. GitNexus
detect-changes reports HIGH risk over 9 execution flows; every one of those
suites is green and no site changed its observable contract.

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(memory): resolve the Ollama endpoint from configuration, not the …

head_commit.message:
fix(memory): resolve the Ollama endpoint from configuration, not the request

The embedding path fetched `options["ollama_base_url"]` straight from the chat
request and POSTed the text being embedded to it, so a caller that reached
those options could point the sidecar at any host and receive memory content.
No client in the repository ever set that key.

The endpoint now comes from OLLAMA_HOST alone, through one shared sanitizer:
http/https only, a host that is an IP literal or DNS-shaped, no credentials,
query or fragment, and the base rebuilt from the parsed parts so userinfo
cannot smuggle a different target past string concatenation. A reverse-proxy
path prefix survives, since Ollama's own API paths are absolute. Invalid
configuration falls back to the local default rather than failing the run.

memory_factory keeps its own copy of the helper because memory_embeddings
replaces it at import time; both are fixed so neither shape can drift back.

Closes the two critical CodeQL py/partial-ssrf alerts.

Verified: 2465 sidecar tests pass, including 24 new endpoint cases covering
credentials, non-http schemes, query/fragment, invalid ports and hosts, and
that request options can no longer choose the endpoint.

head_commit.message:
fix(security): close the first ten CodeQL findings

Supply chain and CI hardening:
- pin azure/login, azure/artifact-signing-action (x3) and
  peter-evans/create-pull-request to commit SHAs so a moved tag cannot reach
  the Windows signing credentials or the README pull-request token;
- give Validate MCP Registry an explicit read-only permissions block.

Code fixes:
- prepare-build-version uses the official semver pattern, whose prerelease
  alternatives are disjoint, removing the exponential backtracking path (it
  also now rejects leading-zero numeric identifiers, as semver requires);
- the test-api route compiler escapes every regex metacharacter in the literal
  runs between :params instead of only "/", so a pattern can no longer compile
  to a different matcher than it reads;
- skill pack extraction creates its temp directory exclusively with mode 0700
  rather than mkdir --recursive, which succeeds on an attacker-planted path;
- the smoke script writes its screenshot under mkdtemp instead of a fixed
  /tmp name.

The three Windows signing tests now assert the pinned-SHA form, which is a
stronger contract than the floating tags they pinned before.

Verified: electron 8834 passed, frontend 5116 passed, release-qa/mcp-registry/
mcp-runtime/notices unit suites green, validate:mcp green; the semver and route
compilers were diffed old-vs-new over the real version strings and route table
with zero behaviour differences beyond the intended semver tightening.

352px wide at the 300px minimum: the input rows now fit, but the output

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(builder): let an input row wrap at the panel's minimum width (#341)

head_commit.message:
fix(builder): let an input row wrap at the panel's minimum width

At the detail panel's 300px minimum an input row's header line
`[name] ← [source] ×` needs about 328px of the 248px it has, so the
agent and End bodies scrolled sideways and the source selector and
remove button sat past the edge (#341 acceptance, four shell units).

The header may now wrap: the name keeps the first line and `← source ×`
moves whole to the next one as one unshrinkable group. Nothing is
hidden, shrunk or clipped and the minimum width is unchanged; at wider
panels the line renders exactly as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

typed as returning None, so every caller looked like it could fall through.
They now build the exception (keeping the `from cause` chaining) and each
caller raises it explicitly. No behaviour change.

head_commit.message:
chore(codeql): clear 48 code-scanning alerts on the sidecar and renderer

Dead module constants and unused imports are removed, modules imported
both as `import x` and `from x import y` keep one form, re-exported names
that tests and sibling modules read through routes.py and memory_factory
are declared in __all__, the raising helpers are typed NoReturn, a
request-provided toolkit name is stripped of line breaks before logging,
and two JavaScript sites drop a redundant null compare and a dead
assignment. No behaviour change; three names first removed turned out to
be module re-exports (character_defaults, REDACTION_MARKER) and stay.

head_commit.message:
security: fix 39 CodeQL alerts and pin the release-QA Unchain ref

- session_guard_migration: read the pending intent through an
  O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW descriptor instead of exists-then-read (fs race)
- test-api /v1/debug/dom: embed the selector as a JS string literal
- route_computer_use: log on/off literals instead of request values
- release-qa fake provider / test-api client: fixed error body,
  validated port file
- memory_vault, vault_sink_job_supervisor, memory_v2_store:
  missing-await, exit-from-finally, implicit SQL concatenation
- _shared-release-deterministic.yml: refuse a UNCHAIN_SOURCE_REF that
  is not a full 40-hex commit SHA
- note-level cleanups: abstract-method docstrings, _OwnedHandle as a
  context manager, unused imports/locals, ASI, dead guards

Local CodeQL (security-and-quality): 302 -> 263 results, no new ones.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
feat: register bug-bounty-intelligence-mcp in the toolkit store

Adds bug-bounty-intelligence-mcp as a needs_review, non-installable
entry per the store's own submission contract:

- Pins the real published npm package (bug-bounty-intelligence-mcp@1.0.3),
  not a github: install spec. The prior issue's install command was
  never a valid registry entry to begin with.
- trustLevel/status both needs_review, installable: false, so nothing
  ships to users before a maintainer reviews it.
- Two tools are free and unconfirmed (list_vulnerability_patterns,
  get_scan_report); scan_contract requires confirmation because it
  starts a paid x402 flow (5 USDC on Base, paid to the author's wallet,
  not billed through PuPu).
- readmeMarkdown states plainly this is third-party and pending review,
  and that the acceptance-rate numbers cover 1,032 exact-reconciled
  findings, not the full training corpus.

Verified with npm run validate:mcp against the actual schema and
catalog invariants before committing.

Closes #186

head_commit.message:
fix: render streamed reasoning deltas as one block per model turn

Anthropic-protocol providers emit one reasoning runtime event per
thinking_delta, and each became its own trace frame. On DeepSeek every
delta is a single token, so one reasoning turn rendered as hundreds of
"Reasoning" blocks and inflated the step count.

Coalesce adjacent reasoning delta frames from the same run and iteration
in TraceChain's displayFrames. This covers live streams and already
persisted chats. Whole Responses API reasoning_items stay separate.

Refs #379

workflow_runs.display_title: feat: add CODEOWNERS and the code owner path

head_commit.message:
feat: add CODEOWNERS and the path to becoming a code owner

Introduces the delegation mechanism designed in
docs/plans/2026-09-29-code-owner-path-design.md.

CODEOWNERS starts with a fallback line assigning every unclaimed path to the
project owner, plus the paths that are never delegated: the release workflows,
CODEOWNERS itself, the MCP store catalog, and the legal files. Assigned areas
are appended one line at a time as applications are approved.

docs/contributing/becoming-a-code-owner.md states the bar publicly: two merged
pull requests in the path applied for, an issue to apply, and the two ways the
role lapses. A code owner may approve and merge inside their path, including
their own changes; main, the release pipeline, and the store catalog are never
delegated.

This file has no effect until require_code_owner_review is enabled on the
branch rulesets.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
docs: drop the Discussions channel from the contributor path

Discussions was added as the optional expression-of-interest channel, but an
inbox nobody intends to watch is worse than no inbox: an unanswered thread
reads as an inactive project.

Interest now arrives as a comment on the issue itself, which is where claiming
already happens, so a task keeps one canonical home and no second surface needs
watching. Questions about a task go on that task. Setup problems and unsure
ideas open an issue.

Removes both Discussions contact links, leaving three guide links on the issue
chooser, and removes the Discussions references from README, CONTRIBUTING, and
the first-contribution guide.

workflow_runs.display_title: docs: add an onboarding path for external contributors

head_commit.message:
docs: add an onboarding path for external contributors

Newcomers had no starting point: the README presented the MCP store as the
only way in, nothing defined `good first issue` or `help wanted`, no rule said
how a task is claimed, and there was no channel for "I'd like to help".

Add docs/contributing/first-contribution.md as the single page all entry points
lead to, covering contribution types, finding and claiming a task, setup, the
base: dev submission flow, and what a contributor explicitly does not need
(write access, label permissions, board access).

Document the claiming rule identically there and in CONTRIBUTING.md: comment to
claim, a maintainer assigns, 14 days without visible progress releases it.

Route interest and questions to Discussions from the issue-creation screen
rather than onto the issue tracker, matching the convention in comparable
projects. Add CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md (Contributor Covenant 2.1).

Repair the README anchor to CONTRIBUTING.md, dead since that heading was
renamed to "Contribute an MCP server, Skill, or Toolkit".

Closes #315

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
fix(agents): category glyphs for the palette, and two menu icon calls (#358)

- The palette's groups carry their own glyph: a route for Steps, the things
  that move the flow along, and a puzzle piece for Attachments, the things that
  hang off a node. Declared in the catalog next to the labels, so a new group
  cannot arrive without one — a test asserts every group has an icon and that
  the key exists in the manifest.
- Select all takes shape-line, the four-handled selection box.
- Fit to view loses its glyph. It and Reset zoom are view plumbing rather than
  actions on the graph, and they now read as a quiet pair: no shortcut and no
  icon on either.

Icons added from Remix Icon: route (Map/route-line), puzzle_2
(Development/puzzle-2-line), shape (Design/shape-line). No SVG was drawn by
hand.

Verified in the running app against an isolated profile: the palette's STEPS
heading renders the route glyph, and the seven corrections from the previous
commit all hold — no menu mid-drag, the detail page closes when its node is
deleted, the view rows are bare, ⌘ draws from the manifest, doorway rows carry
the chevron, Duplicate is gone, and the palette footer uses corner-down-left.

workflow_runs.display_title: feat(agents): target-aware canvas context menus and a node palette (#358)

head_commit.message:
feat(agents): give the canvas a menu per right-click target, and a node palette (#358)

The canvas had one context menu and it was the same everywhere: onContextMenu
sat on the container and reported only coordinates, so right-clicking a node, a
connection or empty space all opened the same three-item "Add" list, and
nothing on it acted on what was clicked.

Resolve the target inside the existing handler — nodes already carry
data-flow-node-id, and the edge hit path now carries data-flow-edge-id — select
it, and pass it through. No new editor API.

- recipe_node_catalog.js: one entry per addable node type (label, group, icon,
  description, ports, creation defaults, id prefix, graph_kinds). ports_for,
  add_node and the palette all read it, so the palette cannot offer a node that
  creation does not know how to build. Graph-kind filtering is written now and
  inert until a recipe carries a kind.
- Three menu builders plus a dispatcher. Groups are fixed, membership varies by
  capability. Delete reads node.deletable, the flag the Delete key already
  reads, so keyboard and menu cannot disagree; Start and End grey out with the
  reason in the row's new trailing slot.
- recipe_node_palette.js: search, grouped results, arrow keys and Enter,
  Escape and click-away. Inserts where the right-click happened.
- recipe_graph_edits.js: "Insert node after…" and "Insert node here…" splice
  into the flow rather than dropping a floating node — outer ports preserved,
  attach connections and non-flow nodes refused.
- ContextMenu: rows gain a trailing slot (shortcut when enabled, reason when
  disabled), and measureMenuHeight replaces items.length * 32, which counted a
  9px separator as a 32px row. The side menu's and recipe list's menus already
  use separators, so they overstated their height and flipped upward early near
  the window bottom; they sit correctly now.
- Escape with a menu or the palette open no longer closes the Agents modal
  underneath it: the menu closes on a document listener, Modal closes on a
  window listener, and the menu is not on the modal stack.
- FlowEditor gains fit_token, zoom_reset_token and select_all_token following
  the existing reset_token idiom, starting undefined so they stay inert on
  mount.

Rename is deliberately absent rather than dead: only the agent node renders a
name today, and the per-type identity table in #341 replaces these node
components, so building inline rename now would mean building it twice. The
builder shows the row only when a handler is supplied.

Tests: 430 suites / 5239 passed on this candidate; base f9c870e6 measured
425 / 5162. CI build compiles clean. Verified in the running app against an
isolated profile.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(agents): align the builder's top strip, share-based panel widths, and reachable window controls (#339)

head_commit.message:
fix(agents): cap each builder panel at a share of the canvas (#339)

The workflow list and the detail panel stopped at fixed widths (480 and
640), which is a different thing on a laptop and on a large display: on a
small window either panel could take almost everything, while on a wide
one neither could use the space.

Each panel now has a share of the canvas instead: the list 35% and the
detail panel 50% (project owner, 2026-09-26). The minimum stays absolute
(200 / 300) and wins when the share falls below it, so a narrow window
keeps the panel usable rather than squeezing it.

- recipe_panel_widths: RECIPE_PANEL_LIMITS carries maxRatio in place of
  max, with panelMaxWidth() and clampPanelWidth() to apply it.
  readRecipePanelWidths() takes an optional container width, so a width
  stored when the window was wider comes back inside the new share.
- recipes_page: measures the canvas with a ResizeObserver, falling back to
  the window's width while the box reports 0 (first paint, jsdom) rather
  than collapsing every panel to its minimum. A container that shrinks
  pulls the panels back in.

Measured live at a 918px canvas: the list stops at 323px (35.2%) and the
detail panel at 461px (50.2%); the extra fraction is each panel's 6px
inset from the edge.

Tests: 423 suites / 5154 passed. GitNexus detect-changes: 4 files,
18 symbols, 6 flows, risk high — every affected flow is RecipesPage's own
panel-width path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
feat(models): prefetch store sizes for the visible rows ±5, capped and cached (#204)

One session-wide scheduler replaces the per-row fetch: at most three tags
requests in flight, de-duplicated, results cached for the session. The
store observes its rows with one IntersectionObserver on the scrolling body
(rootMargin = five rows each side): entering the window requests the tags,
leaving it drops a request that has not started; hover still jumps the
queue. Pending rows show a spinner, never pre-printed sizes.

Measured in the web build: 14 requests on open (9 visible + 5 below), max 3
in flight, 38 after a 1200 px scroll, none repeated.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
Give the Kimi platform row the palette Select variant (#202)

The row copied Appearance's three Select style props but not its
variant="palette". The palette variant owns the dropdown panel's frosted look
and corner radius, so option_style's borderRadius:14 landed inside a default
panel and the option corners fought the panel's — visible only once the dropdown
was actually opened in the running app.

Adds a dedicated guard suite. Every existing test passed with the bug present,
because in jsdom the dropdown never paints; asserting the props is the only way
to catch it. Verified red-before-green: removing the variant fails the guard.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
Add real-app audit evidence for #202

The candidate was driven in an Electron process started from this clone (not the
working checkout, which is what made the #283 audit unusable): shipped sections
visible with enable_custom_model_providers at its default false, saving a key
writing only the secret, the DeepSeek group reaching the model selector, and a
real send landing on api.deepseek.com with HTTP 401 because the probe key was
deliberately fake — everything before provider authentication worked.

workflow_runs.display_title: Ship DeepSeek and Kimi as first-class model providers (#202)

head_commit.message:
Ship DeepSeek and Kimi as first-class model providers (#202)

A shipped preset used to be indistinguishable from a user-authored custom
provider at runtime, so `enable_custom_model_providers` gated both and 0.1.10
kept DeepSeek/Kimi dark rather than expose them half-finished. Worse, the first
API-key save copied the bundled preset into the user's custom-provider store and
the copy won from then on, so a corrected or extended preset never reached
anyone who had already configured that provider.

Both are fixed here without changing one byte of what travels: a shipped model
is still addressed `custom.<slug>:<model>` and still arrives as
`options.custom_provider`, so `parse_custom_provider` and unchain are untouched.

- New `shipped_provider_registry.js` is the single list of shipped providers.
  Adding another costs a registry entry, a preset definition and an icon; the
  settings surface renders from the registry and a test fails if an entry ships
  without either half.
- Definitions resolve from the app bundle on every read
  (`resolveShippedDefinition` / `resolveProviderDefinition` /
  `readRuntimeProviderDefinitions`). `readCustomProviders` keeps its contract and
  only skips shipped slugs, so the editor, import, export and Custom Providers
  list are unchanged. A pre-#202 copy is ignored on read and removed once at
  boot; the stored key is never touched, so a key saved before this keeps
  working with no secret migration.
- The feature flag becomes a per-slug decision at its four call sites instead of
  an early return, gating user-authored providers only.
- `api_key_input.js` and `preset_provider_section.js` — two near-duplicate
  components whose saved states looked different — collapse into one
  `provider_key_section.js` used by all seven sections. At rest a configured key
  is a flat settings row; Kimi's two platforms are a labelled Select row. The
  mask is fixed rather than showing the key's tail, because in the Phase 4
  steady state the renderer cannot read the secret at all.

A shipped provider has no stored definition to switch off, so nothing new is
persisted: clearing the key is how one is turned off, exactly as with the native
provider sections.

BC-002 evidence is artifact-driven: the PuPu suite emits the real producer
output to docs/implementation/ticket-202-evidence/shipped_provider_wire.json and
the backend suite reads that same artifact back through the strict consumer.

head_commit.message:
feat: register bug-bounty-intelligence-mcp in the toolkit store

Adds bug-bounty-intelligence-mcp as a needs_review, non-installable
entry per the store's own submission contract:

- Pins the real published npm package (bug-bounty-intelligence-mcp@1.0.3),
  not a github: install spec. The prior issue's install command was
  never a valid registry entry to begin with.
- trustLevel/status both needs_review, installable: false, so nothing
  ships to users before a maintainer reviews it.
- Two tools are free and unconfirmed (list_vulnerability_patterns,
  get_scan_report); scan_contract requires confirmation because it
  starts a paid x402 flow (5 USDC on Base, paid to the author's wallet,
  not billed through PuPu).
- readmeMarkdown states plainly this is third-party and pending review,
  and that the acceptance-rate numbers cover 1,032 exact-reconciled
  findings, not the full training corpus.

Verified with npm run validate:mcp against the actual schema and
catalog invariants before committing.

Closes #186

workflow_runs.display_title: feat(agents): save native canvas node positions with the Agent

head_commit.message:
feat(agents): save native canvas node positions with the Agent

A drop on the native Agent canvas becomes a move_nodes graph command that
writes the document's display-only layout (skeleton_execution 1.10,
document_layout_v1). The move marks the draft unsaved, Save keeps it, undo
takes it back, and it travels with the Agent. Without that runtime the
canvas keeps the previous localStorage-only behaviour.

Adds the local mirror of the closed layout shape, pruning on delete, a
capture recorded from the real 1.10 validator, the sidecar store round trip
and the contract doc (BC-NL-001/002, SEQ-NL-001).

head_commit.message:
Fold the Subagent Pool into a roster, one entry open at a time

Each entry is a two-line row: its name, how it may be called and what it is
for. Opening one shows its description first, the three call modes with what
each means, then Reads and Memory as segmented choices and Parallel as the
glass switch, with the controls on one pair of edges. The default tool line is
no longer restated, removing moved inside the open row, and adding is one
control with a search and the embedded Agent as its last choice.

head_commit.message:
Make Agents a side-menu drill-in instead of a modal

The side menu's Agents entry now slides the menu into an Agents pane
("‹ Chats" goes back) and swaps the window's centre for the Agents
workspace. The agent list renders in that pane through a portal; the
graph canvas and detail panel fill the content area. The chat stays
mounted underneath, so a running stream and the input draft survive the
trip, and the workspace stays mounted once visited, so returning lands on
the same agent.

- NavigationContext carries appMode and the side-menu slot element
- RecipesPage gains a docked mode (explorerSlot / explorerDocked)
- AgentsModal and its test are removed; nothing opens it any more
- New chat from the Agents pane returns to the chat

head_commit.message:
fix(builder): let an input row wrap at the panel's minimum width

At the detail panel's 300px minimum an input row's header line
`[name] ← [source] ×` needs about 328px of the 248px it has, so the
agent and End bodies scrolled sideways and the source selector and
remove button sat past the edge (#341 acceptance, four shell units).

The header may now wrap: the name keeps the first line and `← source ×`
moves whole to the next one as one unshrinkable group. Nothing is
hidden, shrunk or clipped and the minimum width is unchanged; at wider
panels the line renders exactly as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
refactor(memory-v2): raise repository and invoker failures at the call site

_context_failure, _workspace_failure and _failure always raised but were
typed as returning None, so every caller looked like it could fall through.
They now build the exception (keeping the `from cause` chaining) and each
caller raises it explicitly. No behaviour change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
chore(codeql): clear 48 code-scanning alerts on the sidecar and renderer

Dead module constants and unused imports are removed, modules imported
both as `import x` and `from x import y` keep one form, re-exported names
that tests and sibling modules read through routes.py and memory_factory
are declared in __all__, the raising helpers are typed NoReturn, a
request-provided toolkit name is stripped of line breaks before logging,
and two JavaScript sites drop a redundant null compare and a dead
assignment. No behaviour change; three names first removed turned out to
be module re-exports (character_defaults, REDACTION_MARKER) and stay.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
security: fix 39 CodeQL alerts and pin the release-QA Unchain ref

- session_guard_migration: read the pending intent through an
  O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW descriptor instead of exists-then-read (fs race)
- test-api /v1/debug/dom: embed the selector as a JS string literal
- route_computer_use: log on/off literals instead of request values
- release-qa fake provider / test-api client: fixed error body,
  validated port file
- memory_vault, vault_sink_job_supervisor, memory_v2_store:
  missing-await, exit-from-finally, implicit SQL concatenation
- _shared-release-deterministic.yml: refuse a UNCHAIN_SOURCE_REF that
  is not a full 40-hex commit SHA
- note-level cleanups: abstract-method docstrings, _OwnedHandle as a
  context manager, unused imports/locals, ASI, dead guards

Local CodeQL (security-and-quality): 302 -> 263 results, no new ones.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
fix(token-usage): keep known totals when some receipts have unavailable usage

Settings → Token Usage showed `—` for consumed, input, output and average
tokens and drew no chart whenever a single provider call in the selected
window had unknown usage: useTokenUsageData discarded every total as soon as
one record carried a non-numeric count, while the request count kept
counting all of them.

Sum each metric over the records where it is known, report the number of
excluded requests under the Overview grid, and give an all-unavailable
window its own chart empty state so it stays distinct from an empty window.
The run-bundle projection, IPC envelope and legacy storage are unchanged.

workflow_runs.name: Release QA
workflow_runs.display_title: Render streamed reasoning deltas as one block per model turn

head_commit.message:
fix: render streamed reasoning deltas as one block per model turn

Anthropic-protocol providers emit one reasoning runtime event per
thinking_delta, and each became its own trace frame. On DeepSeek every
delta is a single token, so one reasoning turn rendered as hundreds of
"Reasoning" blocks and inflated the step count.

Coalesce adjacent reasoning delta frames from the same run and iteration
in TraceChain's displayFrames. This covers live streams and already
persisted chats. Whole Responses API reasoning_items stay separate.

Refs #379

workflow_runs.display_title: feat: add CODEOWNERS and the code owner path

head_commit.message:
feat: add CODEOWNERS and the path to becoming a code owner

Introduces the delegation mechanism designed in
docs/plans/2026-09-29-code-owner-path-design.md.

CODEOWNERS starts with a fallback line assigning every unclaimed path to the
project owner, plus the paths that are never delegated: the release workflows,
CODEOWNERS itself, the MCP store catalog, and the legal files. Assigned areas
are appended one line at a time as applications are approved.

docs/contributing/becoming-a-code-owner.md states the bar publicly: two merged
pull requests in the path applied for, an issue to apply, and the two ways the
role lapses. A code owner may approve and merge inside their path, including
their own changes; main, the release pipeline, and the store catalog are never
delegated.

This file has no effect until require_code_owner_review is enabled on the
branch rulesets.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
docs: drop the Discussions channel from the contributor path

Discussions was added as the optional expression-of-interest channel, but an
inbox nobody intends to watch is worse than no inbox: an unanswered thread
reads as an inactive project.

Interest now arrives as a comment on the issue itself, which is where claiming
already happens, so a task keeps one canonical home and no second surface needs
watching. Questions about a task go on that task. Setup problems and unsure
ideas open an issue.

Removes both Discussions contact links, leaving three guide links on the issue
chooser, and removes the Discussions references from README, CONTRIBUTING, and
the first-contribution guide.

workflow_runs.display_title: docs: add an onboarding path for external contributors

head_commit.message:
docs: add an onboarding path for external contributors

Newcomers had no starting point: the README presented the MCP store as the
only way in, nothing defined `good first issue` or `help wanted`, no rule said
how a task is claimed, and there was no channel for "I'd like to help".

Add docs/contributing/first-contribution.md as the single page all entry points
lead to, covering contribution types, finding and claiming a task, setup, the
base: dev submission flow, and what a contributor explicitly does not need
(write access, label permissions, board access).

Document the claiming rule identically there and in CONTRIBUTING.md: comment to
claim, a maintainer assigns, 14 days without visible progress releases it.

Route interest and questions to Discussions from the issue-creation screen
rather than onto the issue tracker, matching the convention in comparable
projects. Add CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md (Contributor Covenant 2.1).

Repair the README anchor to CONTRIBUTING.md, dead since that heading was
renamed to "Contribute an MCP server, Skill, or Toolkit".

Closes #315

head_commit.message:
fix(agents): category glyphs for the palette, and two menu icon calls (#358)

- The palette's groups carry their own glyph: a route for Steps, the things
  that move the flow along, and a puzzle piece for Attachments, the things that
  hang off a node. Declared in the catalog next to the labels, so a new group
  cannot arrive without one — a test asserts every group has an icon and that
  the key exists in the manifest.
- Select all takes shape-line, the four-handled selection box.
- Fit to view loses its glyph. It and Reset zoom are view plumbing rather than
  actions on the graph, and they now read as a quiet pair: no shortcut and no
  icon on either.

Icons added from Remix Icon: route (Map/route-line), puzzle_2
(Development/puzzle-2-line), shape (Design/shape-line). No SVG was drawn by
hand.

Verified in the running app against an isolated profile: the palette's STEPS
heading renders the route glyph, and the seven corrections from the previous
commit all hold — no menu mid-drag, the detail page closes when its node is
deleted, the view rows are bare, ⌘ draws from the manifest, doorway rows carry
the chevron, Duplicate is gone, and the palette footer uses corner-down-left.

workflow_runs.display_title: feat(agents): target-aware canvas context menus and a node palette (#358)

head_commit.message:
feat(agents): give the canvas a menu per right-click target, and a node palette (#358)

The canvas had one context menu and it was the same everywhere: onContextMenu
sat on the container and reported only coordinates, so right-clicking a node, a
connection or empty space all opened the same three-item "Add" list, and
nothing on it acted on what was clicked.

Resolve the target inside the existing handler — nodes already carry
data-flow-node-id, and the edge hit path now carries data-flow-edge-id — select
it, and pass it through. No new editor API.

- recipe_node_catalog.js: one entry per addable node type (label, group, icon,
  description, ports, creation defaults, id prefix, graph_kinds). ports_for,
  add_node and the palette all read it, so the palette cannot offer a node that
  creation does not know how to build. Graph-kind filtering is written now and
  inert until a recipe carries a kind.
- Three menu builders plus a dispatcher. Groups are fixed, membership varies by
  capability. Delete reads node.deletable, the flag the Delete key already
  reads, so keyboard and menu cannot disagree; Start and End grey out with the
  reason in the row's new trailing slot.
- recipe_node_palette.js: search, grouped results, arrow keys and Enter,
  Escape and click-away. Inserts where the right-click happened.
- recipe_graph_edits.js: "Insert node after…" and "Insert node here…" splice
  into the flow rather than dropping a floating node — outer ports preserved,
  attach connections and non-flow nodes refused.
- ContextMenu: rows gain a trailing slot (shortcut when enabled, reason when
  disabled), and measureMenuHeight replaces items.length * 32, which counted a
  9px separator as a 32px row. The side menu's and recipe list's menus already
  use separators, so they overstated their height and flipped upward early near
  the window bottom; they sit correctly now.
- Escape with a menu or the palette open no longer closes the Agents modal
  underneath it: the menu closes on a document listener, Modal closes on a
  window listener, and the menu is not on the modal stack.
- FlowEditor gains fit_token, zoom_reset_token and select_all_token following
  the existing reset_token idiom, starting undefined so they stay inert on
  mount.

Rename is deliberately absent rather than dead: only the agent node renders a
name today, and the per-type identity table in #341 replaces these node
components, so building inline rename now would mean building it twice. The
builder shows the row only when a handler is supplied.

Tests: 430 suites / 5239 passed on this candidate; base f9c870e6 measured
425 / 5162. CI build compiles clean. Verified in the running app against an
isolated profile.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

workflow_runs.name: Release QA
workflow_runs.display_title: fix(agents): align the builder's top strip, share-based panel widths, and reachable window controls (#339)

head_commit.message:
fix(agents): cap each builder panel at a share of the canvas (#339)

The workflow list and the detail panel stopped at fixed widths (480 and
640), which is a different thing on a laptop and on a large display: on a
small window either panel could take almost everything, while on a wide
one neither could use the space.

Each panel now has a share of the canvas instead: the list 35% and the
detail panel 50% (project owner, 2026-09-26). The minimum stays absolute
(200 / 300) and wins when the share falls below it, so a narrow window
keeps the panel usable rather than squeezing it.

- recipe_panel_widths: RECIPE_PANEL_LIMITS carries maxRatio in place of
  max, with panelMaxWidth() and clampPanelWidth() to apply it.
  readRecipePanelWidths() takes an optional container width, so a width
  stored when the window was wider comes back inside the new share.
- recipes_page: measures the canvas with a ResizeObserver, falling back to
  the window's width while the box reports 0 (first paint, jsdom) rather
  than collapsing every panel to its minimum. A container that shrinks
  pulls the panels back in.

Measured live at a 918px canvas: the list stops at 323px (35.2%) and the
detail panel at 461px (50.2%); the extra fraction is each panel's 6px
inset from the edge.

Tests: 423 suites / 5154 passed. GitNexus detect-changes: 4 files,
18 symbols, 6 flows, risk high — every affected flow is RecipesPage's own
panel-width path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
Give the Kimi platform row the palette Select variant (#202)

The row copied Appearance's three Select style props but not its
variant="palette". The palette variant owns the dropdown panel's frosted look
and corner radius, so option_style's borderRadius:14 landed inside a default
panel and the option corners fought the panel's — visible only once the dropdown
was actually opened in the running app.

Adds a dedicated guard suite. Every existing test passed with the bug present,
because in jsdom the dropdown never paints; asserting the props is the only way
to catch it. Verified red-before-green: removing the variant fails the guard.

head_commit.message:
Ship DeepSeek and Kimi as first-class model providers (#202)

A shipped preset used to be indistinguishable from a user-authored custom
provider at runtime, so `enable_custom_model_providers` gated both and 0.1.10
kept DeepSeek/Kimi dark rather than expose them half-finished. Worse, the first
API-key save copied the bundled preset into the user's custom-provider store and
the copy won from then on, so a corrected or extended preset never reached
anyone who had already configured that provider.

Both are fixed here without changing one byte of what travels: a shipped model
is still addressed `custom.<slug>:<model>` and still arrives as
`options.custom_provider`, so `parse_custom_provider` and unchain are untouched.

- New `shipped_provider_registry.js` is the single list of shipped providers.
  Adding another costs a registry entry, a preset definition and an icon; the
  settings surface renders from the registry and a test fails if an entry ships
  without either half.
- Definitions resolve from the app bundle on every read
  (`resolveShippedDefinition` / `resolveProviderDefinition` /
  `readRuntimeProviderDefinitions`). `readCustomProviders` keeps its contract and
  only skips shipped slugs, so the editor, import, export and Custom Providers
  list are unchanged. A pre-#202 copy is ignored on read and removed once at
  boot; the stored key is never touched, so a key saved before this keeps
  working with no secret migration.
- The feature flag becomes a per-slug decision at its four call sites instead of
  an early return, gating user-authored providers only.
- `api_key_input.js` and `preset_provider_section.js` — two near-duplicate
  components whose saved states looked different — collapse into one
  `provider_key_section.js` used by all seven sections. At rest a configured key
  is a flat settings row; Kimi's two platforms are a labelled Select row. The
  mask is fixed rather than showing the key's tail, because in the Phase 4
  steady state the renderer cannot read the secret at all.

A shipped provider has no stored definition to switch off, so nothing new is
persisted: clearing the key is how one is turned off, exactly as with the native
provider sections.

BC-002 evidence is artifact-driven: the PuPu suite emits the real producer
output to docs/implementation/ticket-202-evidence/shipped_provider_wire.json and
the backend suite reads that same artifact back through the strict consumer.

head_commit.message:
feat: register bug-bounty-intelligence-mcp in the toolkit store

Adds bug-bounty-intelligence-mcp as a needs_review, non-installable
entry per the store's own submission contract:

- Pins the real published npm package (bug-bounty-intelligence-mcp@1.0.3),
  not a github: install spec. The prior issue's install command was
  never a valid registry entry to begin with.
- trustLevel/status both needs_review, installable: false, so nothing
  ships to users before a maintainer reviews it.
- Two tools are free and unconfirmed (list_vulnerability_patterns,
  get_scan_report); scan_contract requires confirmation because it
  starts a paid x402 flow (5 USDC on Base, paid to the author's wallet,
  not billed through PuPu).
- readmeMarkdown states plainly this is third-party and pending review,
  and that the acceptance-rate numbers cover 1,032 exact-reconciled
  findings, not the full training corpus.

Verified with npm run validate:mcp against the actual schema and
catalog invariants before committing.

Closes #186

head_commit.message:
feat: register bug-bounty-intelligence-mcp in the toolkit store

Adds bug-bounty-intelligence-mcp as a needs_review, non-installable
entry per the store's own submission contract:

- Pins the real published npm package (bug-bounty-intelligence-mcp@1.0.3),
  not a github: install spec. The prior issue's install command was
  never a valid registry entry to begin with.
- trustLevel/status both needs_review, installable: false, so nothing
  ships to users before a maintainer reviews it.
- Two tools are free and unconfirmed (list_vulnerability_patterns,
  get_scan_report); scan_contract requires confirmation because it
  starts a paid x402 flow (5 USDC on Base, paid to the author's wallet,
  not billed through PuPu).
- readmeMarkdown states plainly this is third-party and pending review,
  and that the acceptance-rate numbers cover 1,032 exact-reconciled
  findings, not the full training corpus.

Verified with npm run validate:mcp against the actual schema and
catalog invariants before committing.

Closes #186

head_commit.message:
feat(agents): save native canvas node positions with the Agent

A drop on the native Agent canvas becomes a move_nodes graph command that
writes the document's display-only layout (skeleton_execution 1.10,
document_layout_v1). The move marks the draft unsaved, Save keeps it, undo
takes it back, and it travels with the Agent. Without that runtime the
canvas keeps the previous localStorage-only behaviour.

Adds the local mirror of the closed layout shape, pruning on delete, a
capture recorded from the real 1.10 validator, the sidecar store round trip
and the contract doc (BC-NL-001/002, SEQ-NL-001).

head_commit.message:
feat(agents): save native canvas node positions with the Agent

A drop on the native Agent canvas becomes a move_nodes graph command that
writes the document's display-only layout (skeleton_execution 1.10,
document_layout_v1). The move marks the draft unsaved, Save keeps it, undo
takes it back, and it travels with the Agent. Without that runtime the
canvas keeps the previous localStorage-only behaviour.

Adds the local mirror of the closed layout shape, pruning on delete, a
capture recorded from the real 1.10 validator, the sidecar store round trip
and the contract doc (BC-NL-001/002, SEQ-NL-001).

New/updated runs outside CodeQL, merge-source enforcement, MCP registry validation and dependency-graph jobs are inspected by attempt. Completed relevant jobs have full log hashes and a scan for gh release download.

reuse.rationale: Reuse documented completed exact-release readbacks while independently checking current identity, all subsequent run metadata, attempts and changed-run logs. No claim that historical logs were re-downloaded.

log_privacy: Only SHA256, byte/line counts, job steps and narrow public command/release-tag excerpts are archived.
